reasoning.title: Use the project’s commit history
reasoning.description: When a GitLab task asks for commits by an author on a particular day; do not rely on the project overview, activity feed, or repository analytics when an exact daily count is required.
reasoning.content: Open the project, choose “Code” and then “Commits,” select the relevant branch if needed, and navigate or filter until the requested date’s commit group is visible. Apply an available author filter when possible; otherwise inspect the author shown on every commit in that date group.

reasoning.title: Count only visibly verified matches
reasoning.description: When extracting an author-by-date commit count from the commits list, especially where dates are grouped, pagination may hide rows, or similar usernames/display names exist.
reasoning.content: Count every visible commit that matches both the exact date and the intended author, continuing through pagination or loading more results until the date group is complete. Open a commit or profile when an abbreviated or near-identical author name is ambiguous, and never infer the count from an unfiltered page or an unseen result.

reasoning.title: Open the branch commit history
reasoning.description: Use this for questions about commits in a GitLab project; do not substitute the Contributors page, which aggregates activity and does not provide a complete date-specific commit list.
reasoning.content: Confirm the project namespace, then expand “Repository” in the project sidebar and select “Commits”; the commit-count link on the overview may also lead there. Verify the branch selector, then paginate or scroll through the date-grouped history until the target date is visibly reached.

reasoning.title: Count only fully verified date rows
reasoning.description: Use this when deriving a count by date and author from the Commits page, especially when the target date spans pagination or author labels are abbreviated or nearly identical.
reasoning.content: Inspect every commit row in the exact date group, continuing until the adjacent date group proves the group is complete, and include only rows whose displayed author matches a requested person. Open the commit detail if a name is shortened, enumerate qualifying rows for each author separately, and report the combined count only after the date, author, and complete row set are visible.

reasoning.title: Open the project’s branch commit history
reasoning.description: Use when a GitLab task asks about commits by date or author within a project; do not rely on the project overview or a summary count that cannot filter the history appropriately.
reasoning.content: Confirm the project namespace, expand “Repository” in the sidebar, and select “Commits”; the commit-count link on the overview may also open this report. Verify the branch selector, then scroll or paginate until the requested date group is visibly reached.

reasoning.title: Count the complete visible date group
reasoning.description: Use when extracting commit counts for specified authors, especially when history is grouped by date, paginated, or names may be abbreviated.
reasoning.content: Inspect every row in the requested date group and continue until the adjacent date group confirms its boundary. Match displayed authors exactly, open commit details if a name is shortened, enumerate all qualifying rows per author, and report the combined count only after the date, identities, and full row set are visibly verified.

reasoning.title: Open the correct commit history
reasoning.description: Use when a GitLab task asks about commits in a project; do not rely on the project overview’s total-commit link or the Contributors report when branch scope, author, or date matters.
reasoning.content: In the project sidebar, expand “Repository” and select “Commits,” then verify the branch selector and switch scope if the question requires more than the displayed default branch. A navigation timeout can still leave the destination loaded, so confirm the “Commits” page and its rows are visible before continuing.

reasoning.title: Count only fully verified matching rows
reasoning.description: Use when deriving an author-by-date count from GitLab’s commit list, especially when results span date groups, pagination, or lazy-loaded sections.
reasoning.content: Inspect the complete relevant history, load every applicable page or section, and enumerate every row whose displayed date and full author name both match; open commit details if a row abbreviates identity information. Keep near-identical names and adjacent dates separate, and report a count only after the qualifying rows—and therefore the evidence for the aggregate—are visibly confirmed.

reasoning.title: Open and verify the correct commit history
reasoning.description: Use when a GitLab task asks about commits in a project; do not rely on the project overview, activity feed, or an unverified default branch.
reasoning.content: In the project sidebar, expand “Repository” and select “Commits,” then confirm the page and commit rows are actually visible even if navigation reports a timeout. Check the branch selector and change scope when required; scroll or paginate through the relevant history rather than assuming the initially displayed branch or rows are complete.

reasoning.title: Count only complete, exact matches
reasoning.description: Use when deriving a count from commit rows by date, author, or another displayed attribute, especially where pagination, grouped dates, abbreviated identities, or similar names can cause omissions.
reasoning.content: Load the entire qualifying date group—ideally through the next date heading—and enumerate every matching row. Match the full displayed author and date exactly, open commit details when the grid abbreviates identity information, keep near-identical variants separate, and report the aggregate only after every supporting row is visibly verified rather than guessed.

reasoning.title: Use the profile’s Contributed projects tab
reasoning.description: Use when asked about repositories the signed-in user contributed to; do not use the dashboard’s “Yours” list, which reflects project membership rather than contribution history.
reasoning.content: Open the account menu, select the visible profile link, then choose “Contributed projects” from the profile tabs. This is the reliable route to the user’s contribution-based repository list.

reasoning.title: Read every qualifying project card and its star metric
reasoning.description: Use after reaching “Contributed projects” when selecting repositories by star count or another displayed metric.
reasoning.content: Sort by “Most stars” when available, then inspect all rows and pages until counts fall below the requested threshold. Verify that the number is the star count by its icon/label, include every qualifying or tied row, and copy the full namespace/repository name from the card or project detail page if the list abbreviates it.

reasoning.title: Open the profile’s contribution report
reasoning.description: Use when identifying repositories the current user contributed to; do not substitute membership-oriented project lists or merge-request shortcuts.
reasoning.content: Open the account menu, select the visible profile link, then choose the “Contributed projects” tab and sort by “Most stars” when available. Do not rely on Dashboard → Projects → “Yours,” and note that the top-level “Merge requests” control may only expand shortcuts rather than show authored contribution history.

reasoning.title: Exhaust and verify qualifying repositories
reasoning.description: Use after reaching “Contributed projects,” especially when names are abbreviated, metrics are adjacent, or results span multiple pages.
reasoning.content: Inspect every row and page until all projects above the strict threshold are covered, confirming the count via the star icon or label rather than its position. Report every qualifying or tied row, open project details when necessary to copy the complete namespace/repository name, and verify similar-looking forks or variants separately instead of guessing.
